solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A POW cell is unlikely to provide a bit of bed linen

indicators.note: unlikely suggests the letters of the phrase come out in an improbable new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner-of-war's cell is hardly a place to expect fine bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' is the anagram signal working on A POW CELL IS; 'to provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fabric cover slipped over a pillow, a standard item of bedding.

clue.text: Design of apparatus inadequate

indicators.note: inadequate says the word falls short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: plant means machinery or apparatus, as in heavy plant

explanation.surface: A complaint that some equipment was badly designed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts the last letter from PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a design or scheme for how something is to be made.

clue.text: No problem for Mr Sprat, being thin

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat, so fatless meat suited him

explanation.surface: Jack Sprat from the nursery rhyme is thin and untroubled.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat is the man in the English nursery rhyme who 'could eat no fat' while his wife 'could eat no lean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat without fat suits Sprat; and a slim person is described the same way.

clue.text: Another Polly working, employed by the company

indicators.note: working means operating or being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A second parrot named Polly has taken a job with the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' is the anagram signal on ANOTHER POLLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone listed among the paid staff is employed by that organisation.

clue.text: Longing to be less than totally cowardly

definitions.note: here a participle, longing for something, which matches the verb to desire badly

indicators.note: less than totally says the word is not given in full, so its last letter goes

parts.note: craven means cowardly

explanation.surface: Someone who wishes to be only somewhat cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than totally' drops the final N from CRAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to long for something is to desire it intensely.

clue.text: Dish desired after battle — soldiers tucked in

indicators.note: tucked in places the soldiers inside the rearranged letters
after a battle things are wrecked and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops tucking into a longed-for meal once the fighting is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after battle' turns DESIRED into SIDEDER, and 'tucked in' puts OR (other ranks) inside after SIDE. 'tucked in' also hints at eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A small extra dish ordered to go with the main course.

clue.text: When suffering setback wimps fret

indicators.note: a setback sends the word backwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: wets is British slang for feeble, ineffectual people

explanation.surface: Feeble people worry when things go wrong for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' reverses WETS; 'When' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a state of anxious agitation; a synonym, as in to stew over something.

clue.text: Kitchen gadgets in store moved outside enclosure

indicators.note: outside puts the rearranged letters around the enclosure
moved means shifted about, so the letters change places

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Kitchen utensils in a shop relocated to an outdoor pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' turns IN STORE into TINOERS, and 'outside' wraps that round PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices for opening cans of food, kept in any kitchen.

clue.text: What offers a domestic structure for children playing

definitions.text: What offers a domestic structure for children playing

parts.words: What offers a domestic structure for children playing
parts.note: a toy house children can play in, named after Wendy in Peter Pan, who had a little house built around her

explanation.surface: Something that gives children a stable home life while they play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic structure' sounds like family routine, but here it is literally a small house. A Wendy house is the British name for a child's playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of a toy playhouse large enough for children to go inside.

clue.text: A very small worker cultivated land endlessly, setting the trend

parts.note: an ant is a tiny worker insect

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: a garden is land that is cultivated

explanation.surface: A tiny labourer who tilled the soil and became a trendsetter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final N from GARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde describes art and ideas ahead of their time, which lead fashions.

clue.text: A new cricket side will get together in a while

parts.note: in cricket the on side, also called leg side, is one half of the field

explanation.surface: A newly formed cricket team will meet up shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (or leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for soon, presently, shortly after now.

clue.text: Girl and boy taken in by illegal seller? It's sure to get heard about

definitions.text: It's sure to get heard about

indicators.note: taken in by puts the two names inside the seller

parts.note: a tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices
Ruth is a girl's name
Will is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl and boy are duped by a black-market ticket seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' (also meaning fooled) places RUTH and WILL inside TOUT, a British word for a ticket scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb saying facts will always be revealed in the end.

clue.text: Study of a heavenly body, dancing angel so hyper

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: An angel, very excited, dances in a heavenly setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges ANGEL SO HYPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The mapping and study of the Moon's surface, from Greek selene, the Moon.

clue.text: Goods in front of cash-receiver not shifting at all

indicators.note: in front of places the goods before the cash-receiver

parts.note: stocks are a shop's goods held for sale
a till receives the cash in a shop

explanation.surface: Shop goods piled in front of the till that just will not sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not shifting' looks like a retailer's lament about unsold stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means entirely motionless, an idiom.

clue.text: Call UFO image phony — not fine one, a sort of optical trick?

indicators.note: phony means fake, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter meant F for fine, but the letters only work if an L goes, as if the clue read line (L)
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Dismissing a UFO photograph as a fake, perhaps a disguise or illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phony' rearranges CALL UFO IMAGE less the letters of 'not fine one'. The setter slipped: removing F (fine) loses the only F, so it is an L (line) and I that must go.
explanation.definitionFit: Disguise that blends with the background tricks the eye, a kind of visual deception.

clue.text: Initially those reinforcements helped and worked hard

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: availed means helped or was of use

explanation.surface: The extra troops at the start proved useful and toiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes T and R from 'those reinforcements'.
explanation.definitionFit: To travail is to labour painfully; a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: A way of being silly with feet all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A clumsy person whose silly feet go everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges SILLY and FEET; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of living, the manner in which someone conducts their existence.

clue.text: Long after sunbathing one may see this dance

parts.words: Long after sunbathing one may see this
parts.note: a long time after lying in the sun, the brown skin colour fades away, read as two words

explanation.surface: A dance you might watch long after a day of sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer three letters in: long after sunbathing, the bronze colouring disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Mostly hard work when one is in group of entertainers

indicators.note: is in puts the one inside the shortened word
mostly drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: a chore is a tedious, hard task
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Most of the drudgery falls on one member of a troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts CHORE to CHOR, and 'is in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a body of singers, who perform to entertain.

clue.text: Get rid of factory producing explosive devices

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them
works means a factory, as in steelworks

explanation.surface: Closing down a factory that makes explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrotechnics, devices that explode for display.

clue.text: Characters held by copper are seen to be so careful

parts.note: the letters inside copper are PP, the musical mark for very quiet, spelt out as a doubled word for gently

explanation.surface: Police officers who are seen to be cautious in their work.
explanation.walkthrough: PP in music stands for pianissimo, very quietly. 'Softly, Softly' was also a British TV police drama, which fits the copper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cautious, patient approach, from the saying about catching a monkey gently.

clue.text: Jack sits in car in a body of water

indicators.note: sits in puts the jack inside the car

parts.note: a Ford is a make of car
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

explanation.surface: A man called Jack sitting in a car that is in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sits in' puts J inside FORD; the second 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow sea inlet between cliffs, as in Norway.

clue.text: Artist makes marks with topless pen

parts.note: M stands for marks, the old German currency

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: An artist making marks with a pen missing its cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops B from BIRO, the British word for a ballpoint. Joan Miró was a Spanish painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Miró, Catalan surrealist painter, is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Caveman a disgrace ousting mother

indicators.note: ousting throws the mother out of the word

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A caveman, a disgrace, driving out his own mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting' removes MA from STIGMA. Stig of the Dump is a British children's book by Clive King about a boy who lives in a chalk pit.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Stig of the Dump is a Stone Age caveman.

clue.text: Rebel army facing question in country

indicators.note: facing puts the army in front of the question

parts.note: the IRA is the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: An insurgent force faces questioning inside a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: What could make cot go slimy? One looks at mouldy stuff

indicators.note: could make says the words can be remade into something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Asking what turns a baby's cot slimy, answered by a mould expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges COT GO SLIMY; 'What' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies fungi, including moulds.

clue.text: Place where a lady powders her nose, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear marks a word heard by its sound

parts.words: where a lady powders her nose
parts.note: to powder one's nose is a euphemism for visiting the lavatory, the loo

explanation.surface: A coy question about the ladies' room.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is British slang for toilet; it sounds like the French-derived word for place, as in 'in lieu of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place or stead, as in in lieu of.

clue.text: Get hard with son terribly self- willed

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Being tough with a son who is dreadfully stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges GET HARD and SON; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate and determined to have one's own way, a synonym.
